clue.text: Cause of bowler's exhaustion?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls from one bowler, so too much effort, or the strain of overs, wears a bowler out

explanation.surface: A question about what tires out a cricket bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls from one bowler; read the answer as OVER STRAIN, the strain of bowling overs, as well as plain overexertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive exertion is what exhausts anyone, a bowler included.

clue.text: Bacchanalia's gory mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of gory are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A drunken revel leaves a gory mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bacchanalia was a Roman drunken festival, hence any wild revel or debauch.

clue.text: Philosopher had very long time with difficult sums

parts.note: an era is a very long period of time

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters of sums are troublesome and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker spent ages struggling with hard arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the Dutch Renaissance humanist; 'had' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a famous Renaissance humanist thinker.

clue.text: Frolic in store?

parts.note: a frolic is a spree, and one in a store means a shopping binge

explanation.surface: A bit of fun planned for the future, or high jinks in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in store' looks like 'coming up', but read it as 'in a shop': a frolic there is a buying binge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping binge is an outing of lavish buying, a bout of fun in a shop.

clue.text: Overdrawn in hire charge — the rat

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, the abbreviation going into the charge

parts.note: rent is the charge paid for hiring property
OD is the banking abbreviation for overdrawn

explanation.surface: A grumble about a rat of a landlord charging rent to someone already in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is a gnawing mammal of the order Rodentia.

clue.text: Entering American company order in middle of night

parts.note: Inc, incorporated, marks an American company
OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its central letter, here of night

explanation.surface: A US firm's instruction arrives in the dead of night.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arriving or coming in is entering.

clue.text: I entered by means of landing-stage

indicators.note: entered means the I goes into the other word

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: Someone arrived via a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetty projecting into water where boats land is a landing-stage.

clue.text: Hard time a region suffered

indicators.note: a region that has suffered is damaged and broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An area went through a tough period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard time' looks like hardship, but it is the age named after the hard metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period when iron tools were made is a time named for a hard metal.

clue.text: Thought it might have been seen in the mirror

definitions.text: it might have been seen in the mirror

explanation.surface: Musing on what the looking-glass shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful consideration is one sense; an image cast back by glass is the other.

clue.text: Energetic signal to proceed

explanation.surface: A dynamic person given the green light.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising, dynamic person is one sense; permission to start is the other.

clue.text: Succeeded, but not as a rider

explanation.surface: Something worked, though not for the jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a rider who fell from the horse failed to stay on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that worked is one sense; tumbling from a horse, so ending up unmounted, is the other.

clue.text: Varied clues Naomi and les solved

indicators.note: solved suggests the letters are worked out and put into a new order

explanation.surface: Naomi and Les crack a diverse set of puzzle clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted or diverse items are mixed in kind.

clue.text: Without any doubt did something correctly

explanation.surface: Certainly someone got it right.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase used as an assurance means certainly; literally it means acted without error.

clue.text: Dabbler, his disposition is lacking professional skill

parts.note: a dabbler is a non-professional

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters of his are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A hobbyist whose temperament shows he is not up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Unskilful work done like a hobbyist's lacks expertise.

clue.text: Thinking it is funny but not to start with

indicators.note: the starting letter of the synonym for funny is not kept

parts.note: amusing means funny

explanation.surface: Someone thinks something is humorous, though not at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pondering or reflecting is thinking.

clue.text: Profitable concern?

parts.note: a concern can be a business, but also a stake, and money lent returns this profitable sum

explanation.surface: Sounds like a business that turns a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concern' tempts as a firm; it is both a share and the money earned on a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a stake one cares about and the return paid on savings.

clue.text: Went on board small ship in eastern sea

indicators.note: in places the vessel inside the other pieces

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
a bark is a small sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone boarded a little vessel in an eastern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding a vessel to set sail is going aboard.

clue.text: Stereo I'm retuning, it is tedious

indicators.note: retuning adjusts the setting, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Fiddling with the hi-fi again is boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome, dull things are tedious.

clue.text: Fundamental liberal

explanation.surface: A basic progressive view.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the root is one sense; a politically progressive reformer is the other.

clue.text: Fate of colt collapsing in front of house

indicators.note: in front of puts the rearranged colt before the abbreviation
a collapsing colt falls into pieces, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The destiny of a young horse that falls down outside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fate' looks like destiny but means one of the three Fates of Greek myth, Clotho being the spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho spun the thread of life, one of the three Moirai of Greek myth.

clue.text: Departed willingly!

parts.note: departed means died, and willingly means with a will left in place

explanation.surface: Someone left gladly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departed' looks like left, but means died; 'willingly' means having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a valid will is so described in law.

clue.text: A maxim that is unprincipled

parts.note: a moral is a lesson or maxim

explanation.surface: A saying that lacks principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Without ethical standards means lacking principles.

clue.text: Clothes that should not be worn out

definitions.text: Clothes that should not be worn out

parts.words: Clothes that should not be worn out
parts.note: worn out means not threadbare but worn outside, and these garments go underneath

explanation.surface: Garments that ought not to be used until shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn out' suggests threadbare; read it as worn on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is clothing worn beneath other clothes, not displayed.

clue.text: Incorrect instruction?

parts.note: read as in-correct, an instruction not to correct; proofreaders mark text to be left as it was

explanation.surface: A wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incorrect' looks like wrong; split it as 'in-correct', an order not to make a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders write this Latin word, 'let it stand', to cancel an alteration.

clue.text: Under restraint wearing tartan?

explanation.surface: Someone kept under control in a checked kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Held back or controlled is one sense; dressed in checked cloth like tartan is the other.

clue.text: City has diplomacy when this is read

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: A city shows diplomacy at the moment a document is read.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to order a crowd to disperse; to read someone it means to scold them.
explanation.definitionFit: Magistrates recited this statute to disperse unruly crowds, so it is the thing read out.

clue.text: First light entering sweltering animal home

indicators.note: entering shows one letter going inside the other word

parts.note: sweltering means very hot

indicators.note: First picks the initial letter of light

explanation.surface: A ray of light gets into a sweltering animal shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter's den is called by this name.

clue.text: An old share's despatched, say, for teenager

parts.note: an gives the letter A
dole is an old word for a portion or share

indicators.note: say signals the following word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sent means despatched

explanation.surface: An elderly person's shares are sent off for a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives SCENT, sounding like SENT (despatched). DOLE is an archaic word for a share or portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth between childhood and adulthood is a teenager.
